definition: Proclivity means a natural tendency or inclination toward something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word proclivity. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know proclivity should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The kitten's proclivity for high places announced itself the day she was found asleep on top of the refrigerator.
A leaning is a gentle pull you can ignore; a proclivity tilts the whole personality toward the thing, visibly and repeatedly.
Compulsion goes beyond proclivity: a proclivity inclines you toward what you would choose anyway, while compulsion drives you whether you choose it or not.

A tendency is any leaning at all, in people or in things — even clouds and markets have tendencies. Proclivity belongs to persons: a natural, built-in tilt of the personality toward one kind of thing, there before you ever noticed it.

A predisposition is a built-in readiness for something to develop, said as often of health as of character — a predisposition to colds or to worry. Proclivity is about conduct: the natural leaning that shows in what a person repeatedly chooses and does.

A penchant is a strong liking — a taste you happily indulge, for loud ties or midnight snacks. Proclivity runs deeper than taste: a built-in tilt of the whole personality toward one kind of thing, showing in conduct since childhood, not just in what pleases you.

Latin clivus, 'slope,' never took root in English on its own - its other descendants, acclivity and declivity, are rare surveyors' terms. Distant cousins from the same ancient 'lean' root did thrive: incline, and even lean itself. Proclivity keeps the old slope frozen inside it.
Proclivity means a natural tendency or inclination toward something.
Every roommate quiz asked the same question in different words, and Dana answered honestly: given a free Saturday, she would reorganize something - the spice rack, the closet, the garage.
A proclivity for imposing order, the survey called it, and it had been visible since her crayon days, when she sorted the box by warmth of color.
Proclivity is more specific than habit or preference: it names a natural leaning - the built-in tilt of a personality toward one kind of thing.
Habits are acquired and can be broken; a proclivity was there before you noticed it, pulling like a slope.
Proclivity is slightly formal and pairs with 'for': a proclivity for order, for risk, for high places.
Say tendency in everyday talk.
Choose proclivity when you mean a leaning that feels built into the person rather than picked up along the way.

Coaches meeting Dara Okonkwo for the first time always asked the same question: who taught her to attack like that?
The answer, her father insisted, was no one.
At six, playing her first tournament, she gave up her queen on move nine because she liked how the board opened up.
Trainers tried for years to school it out of her, steering her toward quiet, positional play.
The lessons held for a tournament or two, then the sacrifices returned.

Analysts eventually stopped calling it a style, as if it were chosen, and started calling it a proclivity: a tilt in the player herself, older than any coaching and visible in every game she had ever played.
Her rivals prepare for it anyway.
Knowing the wave is coming has never made it easier to stand against.
